text:
lina: Heads-up: p99 jump on /v1/generate in the latency dashboard around 08:02 UTC. p50 steady, p95 +20ms, p99 +120ms. Could routing/queue changes be affecting percentiles?

mike: I noticed that spike too. We flipped a minor routing weight EU->dedicated yesterday, but that shouldn't cause a p99-only bump.

sangeet: Is this tenant-scoped? Can you share the slice?

lina: Screenshot pasted in console. Appears concentrated on client_tag: mobile-ios and queue=high-priority.

ashley: mobile-ios traffic bumped from the home-feed canary. Gateway queueing is plausible.

mike: Two poss: 1) our service_time aggregate includes queue_time sometimes, 2) sample_origin changed (proxy hops now included).

lina: The console says "service_time p50/p95/p99" but doesn't clearly say if queue time is included. That's a contract problem.

devx: Short-term debug: can we split the viz by queue_time_bucket and kvcache_hit? That should reveal queue-dominated tail.

mike: Ran a quick sample query: SELECT approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.99) FROM samples WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND client_tag='mobile-ios' GROUP BY queue; result: high-priority p99 = 420ms, normal p99 = 310ms.

paul: Are those raw samples or tdigest rollups? That changes interpretation.

mike: Raw samples from sample_store for the 15m window.

ashley: So queue impact is real. p50 unchanged suggests only a small request subset has big queue_time 10 head-of-line or burst.

sangeet: Telemetry question: do we tag sample_origin (gateway|proxy|backend) on all spans? If not, we should. Dashboard loses origin today and we can't filter.

ops-bot: Note: autoscaler event at 07:58 UTC scaled +2 dedicated workers in eu-west-1.

lina: That scaling after the spike implies a capacity knee. Could be transient.

devx: UX ask: add a toggle in latency pane: "include queue time" default off, with hover explaining what counts, so customers aren't surprised by p99 semantics.

paul: Also update API/docs: clarify that latency metrics represent specific measurements; queue time included only when include_queue=true or when sample_origin=gateway.

mike: Internal note: we emit gateway_total_ms at gateway and backend_proc_ms at backend, but console has been plotting service_time_ms without origin tag. We can change dashboard default to backend_proc_ms.

ashley: Changing default is safe runtime-wise but product SLOs using gateway_total_ms need a migration path.

lina: UX improvement: add a legend badge showing which metric is used (gateway_total/backend_proc/combined) and make it clickable to switch. Small change, big clarity.

sangeet: I'll add sample_origin and queue_time_ms to the sample schema; will open PR today, but needs an announcement.

devx: Once sample_origin exists, console can surface a provenance pill like "origin: gateway" next to percentiles and add a raw-sample viewer link for SE debugging.

paul: Short-term alerting: add runbook step to check queue_time_histogram when route p99 > baseline + threshold to reduce noisy pages.

lina: Actions: 1) sangeet: telemetry fields (sample_origin, queue_time_ms) PR by EOD. 2) mike: dashboard default to backend_proc_ms + metric legend. 3) devx: mock UX toggle + provenance pill. 4) paul: add alert runbook snippet. I'll follow up in this thread.

mike: I'll post a quick patch comparing backend_proc_ms p99 vs gateway_total_ms p99 for the window.

ashley: tagging @growth-product 14 this touches mobile canary metrics.

devx: Add unit tests for the toggle (metric switch preserves time range and aggregation).

lina: Thanks for the quick triage. Marking this for follow-up on the Console UX board. :thumbsup:
